model: HTX1 Series rough duty RH / temperature transmitter (BACnet MS/TP)
equipment_type: Humidity / temperature sensor with condensation monitoring
applies_to: Greystone HTX1 series rough-duty RH/temperature transmitters (PICS model DP0011) with optional pipe-temperature condensation probe, digital input and relay, using BACnet MS/TP.
summary: The HTX1 is a Greystone rough-duty RH and temperature transmitter with native BACnet MS/TP. It reports temperature, RH, dewpoint, wet bulb, enthalpy, absolute humidity and pipe temperature as Analog Inputs; Analog Values handle offset or 2-point calibration, altitude and the relay setpoints and timers; Multi-State Values assign the relay source, and Multi-State Inputs give relay status and error codes.
notes: Points from the object table on page 1 of the setup guide. The guide pages carry an SG-DWXXXBAC-002 footer, but the cover and table are for the HTX1.
Relay setpoint and hysteresis ranges, units and defaults change with Relay Assignment (MV 2), e.g. RH low 20 %RH / high 70 %RH by default.
With MV 2 = Condensation the relay turns on when pipe temperature minus dewpoint drops below the setpoint.
Absolute humidity in lb/ft3 uses a Greystone-specific units code (257), not a standard BACnet unit.
Multistate objects are MSV and MSI in the guide; listed here as MV and MI.

integration.summary: Set the MS/TP MAC in the menu, then read temperature, RH and dewpoint. If the relay is to be switched by the BMS, set MV 2 to Free Control by BACnet and write BV 11.

minimum_points.name: Relay Controlled by BACnet
minimum_points.why: Relay command from BMS (MV 2 must be 1)

minimum_points.name: Condensation Status
minimum_points.why: Condensation detected on the pipe probe

integration.enable: The relay follows BV 11 only when Relay Assignment (MV 2) is set to 1, Free Control by BACnet.
setup: Device instance defaults to 381000 + MAC; it stops following the MAC once written over BACnet.
Choose metric or imperial units for all values with BV 1.
gotchas: Set MV 2 before writing relay setpoints; their units and limits depend on the assignment.
Writing 1 to BV 9 restores factory settings.
2-point calibration points must be at least 5 °C (temperature) or 20 %RH apart.
